newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds trade damped down by supply factors.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds trade damped down by supply factors.

text.p: Activity on the Irish bond market was confined to range-trading on Wednesday lacking direction from European markets and capped by supply ahead of next week's domestic auction, dealers said.
" Really, next week's auction is having a very dampening effect on activity," one dealer said. " We're seeing today the very low volumes we saw yesterday."
He said trade was further hampered by a lacklustre performance in both gilts and bunds.
Ireland's National Treasury Management Agency is due next Tuesday to auction 150 million Irish pounds of the eight percent bond due 2006.

By 1630 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 10 pence from Tuesday's close to 101.90 to yield 6.01 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down 15 pence from the close at 109.45 to yield 6.61 percent.
Dealers said foreign participation in the auction would be minimised by worries over the EMU timetable.
"The whole issue of EMU delay is unlikely to be cleared up by Tuesday and I think that will discourage people from putting new money into non-core markets," one dealer said.

Dealers said European markets were generally quiet as they sought direction, with focus largely on the possibility of a delay in the EMU timetable and hints about monetary policy in statements from U.S. Federal officials.
The Federal economic outlooker, the Beige Book, is due for release at 1900 GMT.
